- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.0), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average for stabilization.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and price drops, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model frequently overreacts to sentiment shifts; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 5-day average) to sentiment-weighted forecast adjustments.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict early in the window (first 5–7 days); reduce first 3–5 forecast points by 1–3% to align with observed lag.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is volatile, model underperforms; increase forecast variance by 10–20% to capture uncertainty.
